_comment: The SHAPE of a real Sarvam Batch STT output file, captured from a live job
(an 82 s 16 kHz mono WAV, language_code en-IN, model saaras:v3,
with_timestamps true) and checked in so sarvam::batch_job's parser
is written against what the server actually sends rather than what the docs
describe -- docs.sarvam.ai documents the download endpoint's WRAPPER (the
presigned URLs) but never the schema of the file behind them.
Field names, types, nesting, units and array lengths are verbatim from that
run. The five timestamp values are the real ones. Only the TEXT is replaced,
with placeholders, so no transcript content enters the repository. Keys
beginning with an underscore are this note, not part of Sarvam's payload;
the parser ignores unknown keys, which is what lets them sit here.
The three things this pins that no document states:
1. `timestamps` is THREE PARALLEL ARRAYS, not an array of segment objects.
2. The array of texts is named `words` but holds CHUNKS -- here five spans
of 100-260 characters across 82 s. It is not word-level and never was.
3. `start_time_seconds` / `end_time_seconds` are FLOAT SECONDS from the
start of the file, and consecutive chunks abut exactly (end[i] ==
start[i+1]).
Also captured, from other live jobs:
- `timestamps` is null (not an empty object) when with_timestamps is false.
- `language_probability` is a float ONLY when language_code was `unknown`
and the server auto-detected; it is null whenever a code was supplied.
- `transcript` equals the chunk texts joined by a single space.
transcript: PLACEHOLDER CHUNK ONE. PLACEHOLDER CHUNK TWO. PLACEHOLDER CHUNK THREE. PLACEHOLDER CHUNK FOUR. PLACEHOLDER CHUNK FIVE.
